instruction:
Compare NASA's Voyager 1 and Voyager 2, ESA's Giotto and Rosetta, and JAXA's Hayabusa and Hayabusa2 using official mission HTML. For each, record the responsible agency, launch date, target and date of the following named milestone: Voyager 1's Jupiter flyby, Voyager 2's Neptune flyby, Giotto's Halley encounter, Rosetta's arrival at comet 67P, Hayabusa's arrival at Itokawa, and Hayabusa2's arrival at Ryugu. Keep date ranges and time zones if stated. Classify each named encounter as a flyby or rendezvous/arrival, and separately identify missions explicitly designed for sample return or deployment of a lander. Calculate the calendar-month separation between launch and the named milestone as 12*(milestone year-launch year)+(milestone month-launch month); show the inputs and rank the six results. This is a month-index difference, not a day-accurate flight duration. Cite the dated mission facts, including https://www.isas.jaxa.jp/en/missions/spacecraft/past/hayabusa.html and its Hayabusa2 companion, and ESA's https://www.esa.int/missions/about-us/directorates/science/giotto-overview and https://www.esa.int/missions/about-us/directorates/science/rosetta/rosetta. Finish with two cautions about comparing travel performance when targets and chosen milestones differ. Do not use live spacecraft-distance counters.

Stopping condition: Stop when six dated mission rows, encounter/return/lander classifications, six shown month calculations, the ranking and two qualified comparison cautions are complete.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Evaluate if the agent collected the requested data for Voyager 1: responsible agency (NASA), launch date, target/date of Jupiter flyby (keeping date ranges/time zones if stated), classification as flyby or rendezvous/arrival, and whether it was explicitly designed for sample return/lander. Full credit if all elements are correct based on the mission HTML, or if the agent clearly reports that specific information is unavailable on the found pages. Partial credit if some available elements are missing or incorrectly extracted. Distinguish sample-return design from lander-deployment design rather than using one combined label.

Evaluate if the agent calculated the calendar-month separation for the missions using the exact formula provided: 12*(milestone year-launch year)+(milestone month-launch month), and showed the inputs. Full credit if calculations are present, use the correct formula, and show inputs for all six missions (or for all missions where the dates were available). Partial credit if the formula is applied incorrectly to some, or if inputs are not shown.

Evaluate if the agent ranked the calculation results. Full credit if all successfully calculated missions are ranked based on the calculated month-index differences. No credit if the ranking is missing.

Evaluate if the agent cited the dated mission facts and included the specific requested JAXA and ESA URLs. Full credit if the required URLs are included (even if some pages are down, provided the agent attempted to use them) and facts are cited. Partial credit if citations are present but the specific requested URLs are missing. Use official mission HTML and do not use live spacecraft-distance counters.

Evaluate if the agent finished with two cautions about comparing travel performance when targets and chosen milestones differ. Full credit if two distinct, qualified cautions are provided. Partial credit if only one caution is provided.
